headline: Revenue surges on broad defense demand, but EBIT dips q/q
summary_short: Karman Holdings grew Q1 FY2026 revenue 51.0% y/y to $151.2 million on broad-based demand across all four end markets, while EBIT rose 115.3% y/y to $21.3 million but slipped 14.4% q/q as D&A and G&A costs rose following the Seemann Acquisition.
summary_long: Revenue rose 51.0% y/y to $151.2M on broad growth across all four end markets — Hypersonics/Missile Defense, Space and Launch, Tactical Missiles, and Maritime Defense (aided by the Seemann Acquisition's submarine and LCAC programs). Gross margin expanded 2.8pp on operating leverage, but EBIT fell 14.4% q/q as D&A rose 122% (Seemann intangible amortization) and G&A rose 23% (payroll, tax/accounting/consulting and integration costs). Net income swung to $7.8M from a $4.8M loss a year earlier, helped by a 9.7% effective tax rate versus a discrete-item-driven -222.0% rate last year. Karman closed the $210.2M Seemann Acquisition this quarter, funded largely by a new $260.1M term note; cash ended at $73.8M and backlog reached $1.03B. No forward guidance was issued in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth across all end markets: Hypersonics/Strategic Missile Defense on strategic-program growth, Space and Launch on order timing, Tactical Missiles on drone/loitering-munitions demand and GMLRS output, and Maritime Defense on the Seemann Acquisition's submarine and LCAC programs.
Gross margin rose 2.8pp on operating leverage and improved operating efficiency, even as cost of goods sold rose 44.0% on higher materials and labor spend to support production growth.

Sequential decline driven by D&A up 122% (amortization on Seemann Acquisition intangibles) and G&A up 23% (payroll, tax/accounting/consulting and integration costs), partly offset by lower share-based comp after IPO-related vesting completed.
Swing to profit aided by a 9.7% effective tax rate versus the prior year's -222.0% rate, which reflected tax expense on a pre-tax loss plus discrete non-deductible items.
Turned positive on higher net income and a smaller working-capital drag than the prior year, which had larger increases in contract assets and a bigger accounts-payable decline.
Cash rose sequentially as $260.1M of new term-note proceeds funded the $210.2M Seemann Acquisition and capex, with financing inflows exceeding investing outflows.

Quarter marked by the Seemann Acquisition close, funded via an upsized Citibank term note; management states liquidity is sufficient for the next twelve months and issues no numeric FY2026 guidance in this filing.
